title: Wodehouse - the Man With Two Left Feet

cognitive_validation.rationale: Because no novum-level difference from the empirical world is present, there is no imaginary science or novel social organization to validate as coherent and immanent.

novum_candidates.description: Henry Mills secretly takes modern-dance lessons from Mme Gavarni to win back his wife's admiration, the central plot device of the comic romance.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: No science-fictional estrangement operates: the reader recognizes a familiar social world of banks, restaurants, and dance instructors. The only 'strangeness' is comic exaggeration (goats as golf hazards, a footless pupil), which is humor rather than cognitive estrangement from an empirical norm.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: The dancing-lesson scheme does govern the narrative logic and plot resolution, but centrality alone cannot make a mundane plot device a novum absent novelty and cognitive validation.

novelty.rationale: Dancing lessons, a professional instructor, and a husband's romantic scheme are wholly consistent with the ordinary early-twentieth-century empirical world. There is no totalizing or world-altering difference from the authorial norm; the entire story unfolds in a mundane, realistic New York.
